dedupe_keys.name: international stormwater best management practices bmp database

description: The International Stormwater Best Management Practices (BMP) Database is a repository of field studies on stormwater control measures, with web tools, performance summaries and monitoring guidance. Its core, the Urban Stormwater BMP Database, holds voluntarily shared performance monitoring data and study-site metadata, so that practitioners can see how bioretention, swales, detention and retention basins, wetlands, media filters, porous pavement and other BMPs change pollutant concentrations and runoff volumes. Separate databases on the site cover agricultural BMPs, stream restoration and urban runoff quality (the National Stormwater Quality Database). The project began in 1996 under an ASCE and US EPA agreement and since 2004 has been led by The Water Research Foundation with ASCE's Environmental and Water Resources Institute, the Federal Highway Administration and other sponsors; Wright Water Engineers and Geosyntec Consultants prepare the data and reports. The first summary in 1999 covered 75 BMP studies and the database now holds over 700 BMPs, mostly in the United States; the 2020 performance summary covers the December 2019 release. Access: the 2023 urban release is available by request, reports are free to download, and copyright rests with WRF, whose permission is needed to copy. A 2025 update led by EWRI, WRF, the Mile High Flood District and Villanova University is collecting new data. Caveats: studies are voluntary and uneven in design, and percent removal is deliberately not used as a metric. Simulation uses: parameterising green infrastructure in drainage and climate adaptation models and optimising BMP selection. Related records: EPA SWMM (model-epa-swmm) and PCSWMM (platform-pcswmm).
